title: Fall of Tenochtitlan

where.name: Templo Mayor, Mexico City
where.note: Marker placed at the Templo Mayor, the main temple of Tenochtitlan, in the historic centre of Mexico City.

summary: The Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan, one of the largest cities in the world, was destroyed by Spanish conquistadors under Hernán Cortés and their allies; Mexico City was built on its ruins.
description: Tenochtitlan was founded around 1325 on islands in the marshes of Lake Texcoco and grew through the construction of artificial islands to cover more than 13 square kilometres, linked to the mainland by causeways. By the late 15th century it was the capital of the Aztec empire.
It contained the palace of Montezuma II and hundreds of temples. In 1521 the city was destroyed by Spanish conquistadors under Hernán Cortés.
context: Mexico City was built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan. The marker shows the Templo Mayor, the main temple of the Aztec capital.

facts.text: Tenochtitlan was founded c. 1325 in the marshes of Lake Texcoco.
It was destroyed by the Spanish under Cortés in 1521.

uncertain.text: The city's population is uncertain; Britannica cites an estimate of about 400,000 people in 1519, and other estimates are lower.
